name: Nepher Robotics
gpu_evidence: README.md:52 ("Requires NVIDIA GPU (A100+ recommended), Isaac Sim 5.1 ... NVIDIA Container Toolkit"); also README.md:31 ("--gpus all") and docker/Dockerfile.sandbox:11 (FROM nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:5.1.0)
notes: Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab robotics sandbox in Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit; no min_compute.yml, no explicit VRAM figure. Only 3 active miners.

name: Synth
notes: CPU-only miner per min_compute (16 GB RAM, 2+ cores). Compose + Dockerfile present, pm2 miner.config.js, uv/alembic. Crowded: 235 active miners.

name: lium.io
gpu_evidence: neurons/miners/README.md:140 ("Executors are machines running on GPUs ... The more executors (GPUs) you have, the greater your compensation"); neurons/executor/docker-compose.app.yml:49 (deploy reservations devices "driver: nvidia")
notes: GPU-rental compute subnet: miner is a broker plus one or more GPU executor machines needing nvidia-container-toolkit and sysbox-runc. No min_compute.yml, no VRAM floor stated; scoring is by GPU model/count.

name: engy
gpu_evidence: docs/MINER.md:68 ("Reference config - 4 x RTX 4090 (24 GB), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8"); docs/ANNOUNCEMENT.md:39 ("~35 GB of weights plus KV cache: 2x RTX 4090 or 2x RTX 5090")
notes: Miner serves an FP8 open model via sglang with TOPLOC proofs; needs FP8-capable NVIDIA (Ada/Hopper/Blackwell), multi-GPU. 24 GB is the per-card figure in the reference config, not a single-card floor. Light validator is CPU-only (docs/VALIDATOR.md:9) but that is the validator role.

name: Yanez MIID
gpu_evidence: min_compute.yml:15 (miner gpu.required: False); min_compute.yml:16 (min_vram: 16 "Increased from 8GB to 16GB for better LLM inference")
notes: min_compute contradicts itself: gpu.required False yet min_vram 16 / recommended 32 with 'NVIDIA A100 or RTX 4090' recommended (line 21) - LLM inference in practice wants a GPU. Plain python install (setup.py, requirements-miner.txt), no docker. 30.9% burn.

name: NIOME
gpu_evidence: min_compute.yml:24 (miner gpu.required: False, no vram keys under the miner gpu block); validator by contrast is min_compute.yml:53 required: True with min_vram 8 (line 54)
notes: Miner explicitly CPU-only (16 GB RAM, 4 cores); the GPU requirement applies to validators only. uv + setup.py + entrypoint.sh, no compose. Only 10 active miners, low prune_rank 15.

name: Gradients
gpu_evidence: docs/miner.md:42 ("Validators clone your submitted repository ... run your training script on validator-managed GPUs"); tests/README.md:18 (GPU tests skipped by default so "local CPU-only development does not need Torch, Transformers, CUDA")
notes: Tournament model: miner ships a training repo/Docker image, validators execute it on their GPUs (docs/miner.md:443 notes image tasks use 1xH100 on the validator side). No min_compute.yml. Iterating on a competitive training recipe realistically needs own GPUs even though the runtime does not. Burn 72.3%.

name: Bitsec.ai
gpu_evidence: min_compute.yml:24 (miner gpu.required: True), min_compute.yml:25 (min_vram: 8), min_compute.yml:26 (recommended_vram: 24), min_compute.yml:30 (recommended_gpu: "NVIDIA A100")
notes: Miner GPU required, 8 GB min / 24 GB recommended. Dockerfile + two compose files, plus plain python path (setup.py, uv.lock). Only 1 active miner and ~50% burn.

name: RedTeam
notes: This clone is the subnet/validator + docs repo; miner node lives in a separate repo (docs/miner/README.md:9 RedTeamSubnet/miner). Miner workflow is: develop a solution, build a Docker image, publish to Docker Hub, submit the commit. No min_compute.yml and no GPU/VRAM statement anywhere in the clone, so GPU need cannot be established from evidence here.

name: Ridges
notes: Miner writes a single agent.py run through the miners/ CLI; miners/baseline-requirements.txt is CPU-only (httpx, openai, openrouter, tree-sitter, pandas - no torch) and inference goes through a hosted gateway, but no file states a GPU requirement either way, so gpu_required stays unknown per the evidence rule. Docker only on the validator/api side.
